title: Choose the landing-page composition
question: The Dispatch Wall identity is fixed. Which composition should become the actual responsive page?

options.label: Balanced Dispatch
options.lineage: service ticket and route map in equal balance
options.thesis: The request form and the local dispatch process share the first viewport.
options.viewport: A large request ticket anchors the left while a local route map and confirmation state fill the right.
options.risk: Two equally strong focal areas can compete on smaller screens.

options.label: Route First
options.lineage: regional route map as the visual thesis
options.thesis: The visitor sees a service request move across the company’s local operating area.
options.viewport: The map owns the center while a compact ticket starts the route and a status rail closes it.
options.risk: The compact request form may feel secondary to the narrative.

options.label: Ticket First
options.lineage: oversized service ticket as the primary action surface
options.thesis: The visitor can request service immediately and still understands every next step.
options.viewport: A large service ticket fills the left; a narrow route lane explains confirmation and technician progress on the right.
options.risk: The form can dominate unless later sections give the brand enough breathing room.
